intro: The Spiritmaster's PvP preset and the three or four other setups Global players actually run, each pulled together from several guides[kr], Korean boards[/kr] and Global character statistics. Each is a separate skill preset: resets are free, and a preset keeps its own skill and Stigma levels.
crosscheck: The other sources back the planner's main build on its core. GamerBlurb, Fextralife, games.gg, AOEAH and Evripides' Global guide all run Summon: Ancient Spirit, Enhance: Spirit's Benediction, Jointstrike: Corrode and Flame Blessing. ExpCarry's 16 October sample of 200 Global Spiritmasters found that exact set on about 35% of them, with the Ancient Spirit on 89.5%, Benediction 79.5%, Corrode 74% and Flame Blessing 49.5%. Elemental Fusion, Combustion and the Fire Spirit come first everywhere: they are Evripides' three level-20 musts[kr] and Inven's Korean tier 1[/kr]. The Fire Spirit is summoned last so it stays out, and Wind and Soul's Cry are left low. The differences: ExpCarry counts Jointstrike: Destructive Attack in about 38% of four-Stigma builds against Flame Blessing's 48%, so it is a common fourth slot rather than an occasional swap (see that build below). Evripides ranks Mental Focus above Spirit Strike in the passives and puts Benediction, Elemental Fusion and Corrode in the macro, keeping five Earth Tremor stacks up before each summon. [kr]A Korean video guide (VortexGaming) rates the Corrode passive as nearly worthless (about 0.019% of total damage per level), where the planner raises it in row 9. [/kr]AOEAH calls Mental Focus PvP-only, which no other source does. GameWith's statistics on the top 1,290 EU Spiritmasters support the planner's Daevanion route: their top 20 all take Nezekan's Combat Speed and Cooldown Reduction, Zikel's Damage Boost and Triniel's Multi-Hit nodes. ExpCarry also notes the 14 October fix to Ancient Spirits at Stigma level 15 or lower that sometimes failed to use their skill.

builds.name: PvP Control (Proxy and Seize Magic)
builds.role: Tanky kiting DPS for arena, 1v1 and small Abyss fights
builds.summary: The PvE core minus the boss-only pieces. It keeps the Ancient Spirit and Benediction, and puts Command: Proxy and Seize Magic in the last two Stigma slots. The Earth Spirit stays out to Taunt, and you win by outlasting. You break their crowd control with Defiance, strip their defensive buffs, Fear them once their Defiance is spent, and let the spirits' damage over time add up.
builds.when: Arena, duels and small-group fights in the Abyss. For large Abyss fights, see the group build below.
builds.popularity: This is the PvP set in four separate guides: Aion 2 Maps, Evripides (his 'Default' PvP set), Fextralife and GamerBlurb. In GameWith's statistics on the top 1,290 EU Spiritmasters, Seize Magic sits on 46% of their bars and Command: Proxy on 27%. ExpCarry warns that public data doesn't show which preset a player uses for PvP.
builds.vsMain: Stigma slots 3 and 4 become Command: Proxy and Seize Magic in place of Jointstrike: Corrode and Flame Blessing. Rapid Scattershot and Spirit's Descent go back to 1, and Soul's Cry and Revitalization Contract go to 10. The Earth Spirit, not the Fire Spirit, is the one that stays out. Defiance moves to the top of the order.

skills.note: Your only crowd-control break; Evripides and Fextralife rush it
Fear, plus a 5 s Root from its pick

378 of 383 points. Rapid Scattershot, Spirit's Descent, Summon: Wind Spirit and Spirit Communion stay at 1. No source gives a full PvP point order: this one follows Evripides' and Fextralife's priorities and Aion 2 Maps' preset

specialties.picks: 10% chance to activate skill when Earth Spirit lands attack, then +20% PvE Damage Tolerance and +10 PvP Damage Tolerance to Earth Spirit
Inflicts Root for 5s
+50% Multi-Hit on hit, and Absorbs 1% HP (Evripides says the +2% Attack stacks rarely build in PvP)

stigmas.name: Summon: Ancient Spirit
stigmas.why: Takes a large share of your damage in PvP too; summon it after Benediction

stigmas.name: Enhance: Spirit's Benediction
stigmas.why: +10% PvP Damage Boost and Tolerance for you and your spirit, and 10% Max HP back on cast

stigmas.name: Command: Proxy
stigmas.why: For 6 s at 5, your spirit with the most HP within 25 m shares the hits you take. Use it against their burst

stigmas.name: Seize Magic
stigmas.why: Strips up to 3 buffs from up to 4 enemies; from 10 it also Seals for 5 s when it removes 3

builds.daevanion: Azphel, the PvP board, runs on its own crystals: 36 from Ereshkigal's Monolith in Season 1 and 110 from the Abyss Shop. Take its core nodes first, then Status Effect Resist (Aion 2 Maps). Guides split on whether PvP Damage Boost or PvP Damage Tolerance comes first, but you get both. GameWith's top 20 EU Spiritmasters mostly took HP, PvP Attack and Status Effect Resist first.
builds.gear: Status Effect Resist on every armour piece. Evripides aims for 100%+ Status Effect Resist, 2000+ Accuracy and about 40% Regeneration. Take Revitalization Contract lines on the necklace and earrings, and intermediate Abyssal Manastones with PvP Accuracy and PvP Attack (or PvP Damage Boost: sources split). Wear the Fierce Battle Amulet in place of the Revelation Amulet, and Brawler Wings, or Talisra Wings until you have them. [kr]Inven's Korean PvP guide puts a high value on HP and Defence for this class, since Proxy adds Defence and potions and shields scale with Max HP. It warns that PvP Damage Boost loses value when your Attack can't get past their Defence. [/kr]Keep a PvP Genus preset.
play: End the spirit line on the Earth Spirit: its skill can Taunt a player, and Defiance can't remove a Taunt. Evripides' PvP macro is only Elemental Fusion then the Earth Spirit; play the rest by hand.
Open with Benediction, then summon the Ancient Spirit, so it takes your buffed stats.
When they open on you: Defiance at once, then Command: Proxy for the follow-up. Don't hold Proxy once their burst starts. Use it when an Assassin's Shadowstrike stuns you or a Sorcerer's Frost lands.

Use Seize Magic after they buff: a Gladiator's Armor of Balance, a Ranger's Mother Nature's Breath or a Sorcerer's Arctic Armor. A Templar's Noble Armor and a Chanter's Guardian Blessing can't be removed.
Make them spend Defiance before Soul's Cry: Dimensional Control's Root or Curse can bait it out. Don't Fear into a Gladiator's Tenaciousness, a Cleric's Salvation or a Sorcerer's Hibernation.
Keep your dodge for engages and for a Sorcerer's meteor, which ignores evasion and block. Kite at range: your spirits keep hitting while you move out.
pros: The tankiest ranged DPS in PvP (Evripides)
Fear and Taunt: control no other class has
Seize Magic answers most classes' defensive buffs
cons: Less mobility than a Ranger and less burst than a Sorcerer
Wins on timing: a cooldown pressed too early or too late loses the fight
Fear is control, not a kill tool, and your only escapes are dodge and Defiance

Aion 2 Maps, Evripides, Fextralife and GamerBlurb use Proxy and Seize Magic, and this build follows them. Evripides and Aion 2 Maps offer Siphon or Kaisinel's Power instead of Proxy, and Corrode against Clerics, Chanters and other healers. [kr]Inven's Korean guide calls Siphon the best PvP Stigma and treats Kaisinel's Power as core, but Korea has six Stigma slots to Global's four. Proxy lasts 6 s at Stigma level 5 in the client data that Aion 2 Maps and Fextralife quote; Evripides says 7 s. For the Attack title, Evripides takes Treading on White Wings (PvP Accuracy, PvP Attack, 5.5% PvP Damage Boost), and Aion 2 Maps takes Saint of Ereshkigal (4% PvP Damage Boost).

builds.name: PvE Destructive Attack
builds.summary: The main PvE build with Jointstrike: Destructive Attack in Flame Blessing's slot. It does 50 stagger damage, charging to 55, 60 and 65 from Stigma level 5, the most of any Spiritmaster skill. At higher Stigma levels it hits harder: always a critical hit at 15, and at 20 its first hit resets Curse and Corrode.
builds.when: Stagger checks, and bosses where your party runs out of time on the stagger gauge. Some top players also run it on Transcendence bosses once the Stigma is levelled.
builds.popularity: ExpCarry counted it in about 38% of 172 public four-Stigma Global builds, against Flame Blessing's 48%. GameWith shows it on 45% of the top 1,290 EU Spiritmasters' bars[kr], and in Korea, with six slots, it is part of the standard PvE set (Inven)[/kr].
builds.vsMain: Only Stigma slot 4 changes: Destructive Attack at 5 in place of Flame Blessing. Skill points, Specialties and the macro stay the same. Destructive Attack goes on its own key and is held to charge.

skills.note: Fire it in the stagger windows this build opens
Same 378 points as the main build; 5 spare

specialties.picks: As the main build: Extra damage after 3s on hit, and +10 all Element Boost on hit. Don't take its charge pick
As the main build: up to 12% more damage when fewer targets are hit, and +20% Skill Speed
Restores 120 MP; at 16, -1s all skill cooldowns on hit

builds.daevanion: Same as the main build's route.
builds.gear: Same as the main build. Arcana and Stigma Shards go to Destructive Attack after the Ancient Spirit and Benediction, toward its level-20 reset.
play: Open as usual: Benediction, then the Ancient Spirit, then the macro. Fire Destructive Attack a few seconds after the Ancient Spirit lands.
Fire it only once Corrode and Curse have gone out: a Jointstrike overwrites the one before, and at 20 its reset is wasted on skills that are already ready.
Let go of the macro key while you charge it. A Korean post found the macro firing a freshly reset Curse and cutting the charge short (AOEAH).
Keep it off the macro: a macro step fires a charge skill at its first stage. Save it for when the stagger gauge opens.
pros: Your biggest stagger tool, for stagger-check bosses
Grows stronger with Stigma investment, where Flame Blessing is the simpler default (ExpCarry)
cons: One more manual press, held and timed
Weak until it has Stigma levels

[/kr]The cost is a fourth 150-MP summon every 15 s, and its Specialties need skill levels the planner's route doesn't give.

builds.popularity: Aion 2 Maps finds it on close to half of Global's top Spiritmasters. GameWith shows the Wind Spirit on 85% of the top 1,290 EU Spiritmasters' bars, but at an average skill level of only 7.5. Most guides (Evripides, GamerBlurb[kr], Inven's Korean summary[/kr]) drop it at endgame.

If MP runs dry, drop back to three spirits for the fight.

builds.summary: A safer, sustain-first version of the same engine for solo play. Siphon is in a Stigma slot for HP and MP. Elemental Fusion turns into an area skill for packs, the MP-saving picks stay in, and the Wind Spirit is raised in place of Rapid Scattershot, which only hits staggered targets.

builds.daevanion: The planner's while-levelling route is unchanged: Elemental Fusion and Combustion on every board, the Fire Spirit and Cold Shock on Nezekan and Zikel, and the Combat Speed and Damage Boost core nodes.
builds.gear: Enough Accuracy that pulls don't miss, then Attack and MP sustain. Raise HP and Defence for hard solo content (games.gg).
play: End on the spirit the pull needs: Fire for packs, Earth for a tough enemy (it draws the attacks), Water when MP is low, Wind when HP is low.
Take Corrode out of the macro on trash: it goes off on weak mobs and its cooldown drifts.
Don't overpull: repeated deaths cost more than bigger pulls save (games.gg, GamerBlurb).
Swap Siphon back to Flame Blessing once you survive comfortably (GamerBlurb).

Area Elemental Fusion and the Fire Spirit clear packs
The same engine as the boss build, so nothing new to learn
cons: Lower single-target damage than the main build
The area pick weakens Elemental Fusion on bosses
Needs a preset swap before dungeons
